reviewedReaderValues.name: Dutch Studies

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Dutch Studies degree is designed for non-native speakers of Dutch. It develops advanced Dutch language skills alongside the literature, history, art and society of the Netherlands, culminating in a supervised thesis normally written in Dutch.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The supported curriculum shown totals 165 EC: 115 distinct EC from the first two years, 10 EC of advanced academic reading and writing, a 10 EC thesis, and 30 EC of elective study. The thesis seminar is compulsory and carries no separate credits. A repeated second-year course and conflicting third-year concentration credits leave the full curriculum and UCR comparison unfinished.

curriculum.limitation: Supported subset: 165 of 180 EC. The distinct replacement for a repeated 5 EC second-year course, the third-year concentration allocation and the complete timetable for this entrant cohort still need confirmation.

componentNotes.dst1-04: Part of the first-semester beginner language course. Students enrol in the zero-credit language class and its three credited writing/grammar, reading/vocabulary and speaking/listening examinations together; the class adds no extra credits.
componentNotes.dst1-05: Taken with the beginner writing/grammar and speaking/listening components, rather than as a standalone examination.
componentNotes.dst1-06: Taken with the beginner writing/grammar and reading/vocabulary components, rather than as a standalone examination.
componentNotes.dst1-09: Writing begins from approximately A2 Dutch. Reading/Vocabulary 1B is taken in parallel unless the required level is already demonstrated.
componentNotes.dst1-10: Entry requires at least A2 reading proficiency in Dutch.
componentNotes.dst1-11: Speaking and listening begin from approximately A2 Dutch. Reading/Vocabulary 1B is taken in parallel unless the required level is already demonstrated.
componentNotes.dst1-08: Designed for non-native speakers with basic Dutch at approximately A2/B1. Successful completion also forms part of the programme’s first-year study-advice requirements.
componentNotes.dst2-01: The programme’s ordered progression requires a pass in Writing/Grammar 1B before this introduction to second-language acquisition.
componentNotes.dst2-02: Entry requires a pass in first-year Speaking/Listening 1B.
componentNotes.dst2-05: Entry requires a pass in first-year Writing/Grammar 1B.
componentNotes.dst2-06: Entry requires passes in first-year Writing/Grammar 1B and Reading/Vocabulary 1B.
componentNotes.dst2-07: Entry requires a pass in first-year Reading/Vocabulary 1B.
componentNotes.dst2-10: Entry requires a pass in Writing about Culture, Language Acquisition II.
componentNotes.dst3-5813valsy: Taken after all Language Acquisition II components. The 10 EC comprises 5 EC for independent reading and an oral examination, and 5 EC for processing academic literature in spoken and written Dutch. It prepares students for the thesis.
componentNotes.dst3-5813vscr3y: Entry requires completion of all first- and second-year components and Academic Reading and Writing, Language Acquisition III. Students conduct independent research with supervision, normally writing in Dutch on a language or culture topic. The compulsory thesis seminar has the same entry requirements and carries 0 EC. Participation, including presenting the research at the programme’s student symposium, is required for the thesis credits. The complete cohort timetable remains under review.
componentNotes.dst3-elective-space-30: 30 EC of a minor, approved courses, study abroad or an approved internship within the elective space. Courses must have sufficient level and avoid overlap with the required curriculum; Honours College courses cannot count. Recognized 30 EC minors at Leiden, Delft or Erasmus generally need no separate approval, subject to programme-specific overlap rules. An individual course package requires approval and normally allows at most 10 EC at level 100 and requires at least 10 EC at level 300 or above. Overlapping courses in the Second Language Acquisition or Digital Humanities and Artificial Intelligence minors require approved replacements.
